section.title: Measured app rules
section.intro: Rules for one app's folders, from [`rules/90-apps.json`](https://github.com/midhunkrishna/deepyellow/blob/master/rules/90-apps.json). Each was measured in a macOS virtual machine: the app was used, quit, the folder moved to the Trash, and the app relaunched to see what came back and whether it stayed signed in. The **Measured** line records what was seen.

rules.title: Slack's web cache
rules.whatItIs: Images, files and pages Slack downloaded so it can show them again without fetching them.
rules.consequence: Slack downloads them again as you open them, and you stay signed in.
rules.source: Measured: removed and relaunched Slack 4.53 on macOS 15.7

evidence.observed: Reached 55 MB after about 2 hours of use and grew by about 1 MB a minute while reading channels. After removal Slack relaunched signed in; the folder came back at 0.5 MB and reached 2.5 MB after 5 channels.

rules.title: Slack's logs
rules.whatItIs: Text logs Slack writes while it runs, used to troubleshoot problems.
rules.consequence: Slack starts new logs and you stay signed in.
rules.source: Measured: removed and relaunched Slack 4.53 on macOS 15.7

evidence.observed: Three log files reached 6.5 MB after about 2 hours of use, 2.1 MB of it in 6 minutes of switching channels, with no rotated copies. After removal Slack relaunched signed in and wrote 0.4 MB of new logs.

rules.title: Slack's offline app copy
rules.whatItIs: A copy of Slack's web app that Slack downloads after you sign in, so it can start without the network.
rules.consequence: Slack downloads it again as soon as it starts, so the space is taken again within a minute.
rules.source: Measured: removed and relaunched Slack 4.53 on macOS 15.7

evidence.observed: Appeared at 83 MB right after sign-in and stayed at that size through further use. After removal Slack relaunched signed in and the folder was back at 83 MB within 25 seconds.

rules.title: Safari's web cache
rules.whatItIs: Pages, images and video Safari downloaded so it can show them again without fetching them.
rules.consequence: Safari downloads them again as you browse, and your history and bookmarks stay.
rules.source: Measured: removed and relaunched Safari 18.6 on macOS 15.7

evidence.observed: Reached 552 MB after 60 page views of 30 public sites in 13 minutes. After removal Safari relaunched normally with its history file unchanged; the folder came back at 0.1 MB and reached 74 MB after 8 pages.

rules.title: What websites store in Safari
rules.whatItIs: Data websites keep in Safari, such as saved settings, offline copies and site databases.
rules.consequence: Websites lose what they stored on this Mac, such as settings and offline data.
rules.source: Measured: removed and relaunched Safari 18.6 on macOS 15.7

evidence.observed: Reached 42 MB after 60 page views without signing in to any site. After removal Safari relaunched normally; the folder came back at 0.7 MB and reached 12 MB after 8 pages. Sign-ins to websites were not tested.

rules.title: Safari's history and tabs
rules.whatItIs: Safari's browsing history, open tabs, per-site settings and AutoFill data.
rules.consequence: It deletes your browsing history, tabs and site settings.
rules.source: Measured: folder contents listed in Safari 18.6 on macOS 15.7

evidence.observed: Holds History.db, SafariTabs.db, PerSitePreferences.db and AutoFill databases; 36 MB after 60 page views, 12 MB of it AutoFill corrections.

rules.title: Chrome's downloaded components
rules.whatItIs: Models, voices and lists Chrome downloads in the background for features such as Safe Browsing, read aloud and search suggestions.
rules.consequence: Chrome downloads them again within minutes, so the space is taken again.
rules.source: Measured: removed and relaunched Chrome 157 on macOS 15.7

evidence.observed: Took 147 MB after the first launch and 60 page views. After removal Chrome relaunched normally and downloaded 132 MB of it again within 6 minutes.

rules.title: Spotify's streaming cache
rules.whatItIs: Songs Spotify streamed, kept so they play again without downloading, plus the cache of its built-in browser.
rules.consequence: Spotify streams songs again as you play them, and you stay signed in.
rules.source: Measured: removed and relaunched Spotify 1.3.8 on macOS 15.7

evidence.observed: Reached 334 MB after 40 tracks in 14 minutes, 240 MB of it streamed audio. After removal Spotify relaunched signed in; the folder came back at 57 MB and reached 248 MB after 6 more tracks.

rules.title: Spotify's account database
rules.whatItIs: A database Spotify keeps for each signed-in account.
rules.consequence: Spotify rebuilds it and you stay signed in, though it forgot what was playing.
rules.source: Measured: removed and relaunched Spotify 1.3.8 on macOS 15.7

evidence.observed: Reached 28 MB after 40 tracks on a free account. After removal Spotify relaunched signed in with nothing queued; the folder came back at 8 MB and reached 10 MB after 6 tracks. Songs downloaded for offline listening (Premium) were not tested.

rules.title: VS Code's extension installer cache
rules.whatItIs: Copies of the installer files of extensions VS Code has installed.
rules.consequence: Your extensions stay installed and keep working.
rules.source: Measured: removed and relaunched VS Code 1.145 on macOS 15.7

evidence.observed: Reached 174 MB after installing 6 extensions (9 with their dependencies). After removal VS Code relaunched with all 9 extensions installed, and the folder stayed empty after opening a project.

rules.title: VS Code's compiled code cache
rules.whatItIs: JavaScript that VS Code and its extensions compiled, kept so later starts are faster.
rules.consequence: VS Code compiles it again on its next start, which makes that start slower.
rules.source: Measured: removed and relaunched VS Code 1.145 on macOS 15.7

evidence.observed: Was 15 MB after the first launch. After removal VS Code relaunched normally and rebuilt it at 86 MB right away, now including the installed extensions.

rules.title: VS Code's logs
rules.whatItIs: Text logs VS Code and its extensions write while they run, used to troubleshoot problems.
rules.consequence: VS Code starts new logs, and your settings and extensions stay.
rules.source: Measured: removed and relaunched VS Code 1.145 on macOS 15.7

evidence.observed: Reached 1.1 MB after opening 5 projects. After removal VS Code relaunched normally and wrote 0.2 MB of new logs.

rules.title: VS Code extensions
rules.whatItIs: The extensions installed in VS Code, including the language tools and libraries they bundle.
rules.consequence: Removing files inside breaks the extensions that own them.
rules.sideCondition: Uninstall extensions from the Extensions view in VS Code instead.
rules.source: Measured: folder contents listed in VS Code 1.145 on macOS 15.7

evidence.observed: 6 extensions took 528 MB, 274 MB of it the C/C++ extension. Generic rules matched folders inside them, such as a node_modules bundled with Prettier, where removal would break the extension.

rules.title: Zoom's downloaded components
rules.whatItIs: Speech recognition models for captions and an embedded web engine that Zoom downloads in the background.
rules.consequence: Zoom downloads them again as soon as it starts, so the space is taken again within minutes.
rules.source: Measured: removed and relaunched Zoom 7.2.5 on macOS 15.7

evidence.observed: Took 498 MB after one session with captions: 217 MB of speech models and 281 MB of web engine. After removal Zoom relaunched signed in and downloaded 464 MB of it again within 90 seconds. On a Mac used for months the speech models were 407 MB, all downloaded in the same month.

rules.title: Zoom's program files
rules.whatItIs: Part of the Zoom app itself, unpacked here on first launch and extended with downloaded features.
rules.consequence: Zoom puts the files back the next time it starts, so no space stays free.
rules.source: Measured: removed and relaunched Zoom 7.2.5 on macOS 15.7

evidence.observed: First launch unpacked 148 MB here and it reached 276 MB. After removal Zoom relaunched signed in and had put back 196 MB within 90 seconds.

rules.title: Zoom's account data
rules.whatItIs: Zoom's databases for the signed-in account, meetings and settings.
rules.consequence: Zoom signs you out and starts as if it were newly installed.
rules.source: Measured: removed and relaunched Zoom 7.2.5 on macOS 15.7

evidence.observed: Reached 189 MB after one session, and 260 MB on a Mac used for months. After removal Zoom relaunched signed out, showing its first-run screen, and the folder came back at 2.3 MB.

rules.title: Teams' web cache
rules.whatItIs: Images, files and pages Teams downloaded so it can show them again without fetching them.
rules.consequence: Teams downloads them again as you open them, and you stay signed in.
rules.source: Measured: removed and relaunched Teams 26289 on macOS 15.7

evidence.observed: Reached 85 MB after sign-in and 10 minutes of use with a personal account. After removal Teams relaunched signed in and the folder came back at 2.4 MB.

rules.title: Teams' offline app copy
rules.whatItIs: A copy of the Teams web app that Teams downloads after you sign in, so it can start quickly and without the network.
rules.consequence: Teams downloads it again as soon as it starts, so the space is taken again within a minute.
rules.source: Measured: removed and relaunched Teams 26289 on macOS 15.7

evidence.observed: Was 387 MB right after signing in with a personal account. After removal Teams relaunched signed in and the folder was back at 408 MB within 60 seconds. Work and school accounts were not tested.

rules.title: Teams' logs
rules.whatItIs: Text logs Teams writes while it runs, used to troubleshoot problems.
rules.consequence: Teams starts new logs and you stay signed in.
rules.source: Measured: removed and relaunched Teams 26289 on macOS 15.7

evidence.observed: Reached 6 MB after sign-in and 10 minutes of use. After removal Teams relaunched signed in and wrote 3.7 MB of new logs within a minute.

rules.title: Teams' app data
rules.whatItIs: Everything Teams keeps for your account on this Mac: chats, settings, the offline app copy and caches.
rules.consequence: Teams signs you out and downloads everything again after you sign back in.
rules.source: Measured: removed and relaunched Teams 26289 on macOS 15.7

evidence.observed: Was 540 MB after sign-in and 10 minutes of use. After removing it and the shared Teams group container, Teams relaunched signed out, offering the remembered account, and the folder came back at 28 MB.

rules.title: Discord's web cache
rules.whatItIs: Images, GIFs and pages Discord downloaded so it can show them again without fetching them.
rules.consequence: Discord downloads them again as you open channels, and you stay signed in.
rules.source: Measured: removed and relaunched Discord 0.0.421 on macOS 15.7

evidence.observed: Reached 29 MB after sign-in and 10 minutes in a public community, growing by 18 MB during that use. After removal Discord relaunched signed in and the folder came back at 17 MB within a minute.

rules.title: Discord's program modules
rules.whatItIs: Part of the Discord app itself, such as voice and noise suppression, downloaded on first launch.
rules.consequence: Discord stops starting with a fatal error, and does not download the files again.
rules.source: Measured: removed and relaunched Discord 0.0.421 on macOS 15.7

evidence.observed: Took 224 MB after first launch and use, including a 111 MB voice module. After removal Discord showed 'Cannot find module discord_desktop_core' on two launches in a row; putting the folder back from the Trash fixed it, still signed in.
